title: PRD and launch acceptance playbook for conversational + vector hosted endpoints
creator: Asha Narang
description: This ticket defines the product requirements, acceptance criteria, and launch playbook for the new conversational (chat/completions) and vector (embeddings + rerank) hosted endpoint bundle. The goal is a single, opinionated launch package that satisfies developer ergonomics, production SLAs, and evaluation-quality thresholds for early customers and PLG signups.
background: Customers are asking for a cohesive hosted offering that makes it straightforward to run chat, single-turn completions, dense vector retrieval, and reranking with predictable latency and cost. Engineering has delivered runtime improvements (batching, prefix cache) and model variants; PM must lock scope, define measurable acceptance gates, and coordinate cross-functional rollout with Console, SDKs, and docs.
goals: Ship a minimal, backwards-compatible endpoint bundle that supports conversational streaming, synchronous completions, embeddings, and an end-to-end rerank flow
Define and verify performance & quality SLAs for GA: latency, throughput, availability, and ranking fidelity
Provide a clear launch checklist and rollback criteria for engineering and support teams
Enable SDK and Console features required for discoverability, cost visibility, and per-route observability
scope_in: Hosted conversational endpoint supporting streaming + non-streaming output
Embeddings endpoint with deterministic vectorization and stable dimension contracts
Rerank helper endpoint that accepts candidate lists + embeddings and returns scored ranking
Per-route cost & latency metrics surfaced in Console
Canary rollout with traffic weighting and auto-fallback to compatible model variants
scope_out: Self-hosted / Private (VPC/on-prem) packaging for this bundle (handled by private-2026 roadmap)
Built-in vector DB: we provide vectors only; managed vector DB integrations are future work
Large-scale A/B experiment platform for rerank variants (analytics team to own later)
Model training or fine-tuning flows — only serving and model selection for inference
acceptance_criteria: API contract: OpenAPI/SDK parity documented and validated by automated contract tests
Latency: p95 completion latency <= 180ms for text-completions (single-turn, default model), p95 streaming first-byte < 80ms and token p95 <= 90ms under standard dev plan traffic profile
Embeddings: 90th percentile generation time <= 60ms; vector dimension and dtype stable; sample reproducibility within 1e-6 for identical inputs
Rerank quality: NDCG@10 >= 0.72 on internal standard corpus (eval set v3) for the default rerank model; and at least no regression vs baseline rerank v1
Availability: 99.9% per-route availability during the 14-day post-launch monitoring window
Throughput: Sustained throughput of 250 rps for completions across the hosted pool in the canary cluster without queue growth
Observability: Token-level cost, p50/p95 latency, model variant breakdown, and per-request trace ID appear in Console and link to traces
Security & compliance: KMS integration validated for customer data at rest; audit events emitted for model version changes
SDKs: Node and Python SDKs have examples and end-to-end integration tests exercising streaming, embeddings, and rerank calls
Docs: PRD -> public dev docs + quickstart, labeled GA with migration notes if any behavior differs from legacy endpoints
Operational runbook: Canary rollback steps and severity-to-action map published and acknowledged by SRE and Support
milestones: 2026-03-05: Finalize PRD and acceptance metrics (this ticket)
2026-03-12: Engineering API contract & integration test runner ready
2026-03-22: Internal canary (10% traffic, internal customers) and first quality signoff
rollout_steps: Pre-launch: Run integration smoke tests across SDKs, Console links, and billing metrics
Canary 0-2%: Synthetic traffic and internal users validate latency and correctness; run rerank evals daily
Canary 10%: Add a small set of external beta customers; verify cost telemetry and SLOs
Gradual ramp: 10% -> 50% over 72 hours if all gates pass; SRE to monitor queue growth, autoscaling behavior, and error rates
GA: Open to public signups; enable advanced observability flags for first 30 days
risks: Quality regressions in rerank that are not caught by coarse unit tests — mitigated by daily NDCG runs and a quick revert path
Unexpected latency regressions under real-world prompt distributions — mitigated by synthetic replay from production traces
Billing/cost surprises for customers due to changed token accounting on streaming responses — mitigated by early docs + console cost preview
SDK parity gaps leading to developer friction — mitigated by cross-functional SDK smoke test suite
dependencies: ENG-78120: Serving runtime batching & KV cache uplift (required for p95 targets)
ENG-79211: Streaming SDK encoding and progress callback standardization
ENG-79999: Console cost breakdown augmentation (token-level attribution)
SEC-1201: KMS integration & audit event schema completion
qa_plan: Contract tests: run OpenAPI-based contract suite for each SDK nightly
Regression evals: run rerank NDCG job against eval-set-v3 daily during canary
Chaos test: simulate worker loss and verify graceful fallback to compatible model variants
Cross-team acceptance: PM, Design, Eng, SRE, and Support perform a dry-run of the runbook
telemetry_and_alerts: SLO dashboards: per-route p50/p95 latency, error rate, availability
Alerts: p95 latency breach (>= 180ms) sustained for 5m; error rate > 0.5% for 15m; queue depth growth > 20% over 10m
Cost anomalies: token spend increase > 25% week-over-week for a customer triggers investigator workflow
